title: Unable to type into the terminal, only return key is accepted?
body: I cannot type into Alacritty; only the Return key is accepted. Deleting my configuration so Alacritty starts with defaults does not change the behavior. It had been working before this started, without any changes to the configuration or application. I am on macOS using an Intel MacBook Pro with a Swedish keyboard. The problem occurs with both a build from master and 0.12 RC1. Running with --print-events produces HIToolbox/AppKit traces involving menu-bar handling.

symptoms_visible: I cannot type normal characters into Alacritty; only the Return key is accepted.
The same behavior occurs after deleting my configuration and with both a master build and 0.12 RC1.
The event output prints HIToolbox and AppKit stack traces.
N0.label: N0 keyboard input failure reported

symptoms_visible: I still cannot type when Alacritty is launched with /dev/null as its configuration.
The event log continues to print HIToolbox traces while mouse and redraw events are emitted.
N1.label: N1 default configuration and environment checked

symptoms_visible: After stopping the Yabai services through Brew, I still cannot type into Alacritty.
N1_x.label: N1_x Yabai-disable aftermath

symptoms_visible: Alacritty 0.11 accepts normal typing, while the affected Alacritty build still does not.
The latest winit master example prints KeyboardInput and ReceivedCharacter events when I type.
N2.label: N2 version and winit behavior compared

symptoms_visible: I can type when the updated code is launched with cargo run or cargo run --release.
When I package the same code as Alacritty.app and copy it to Applications, normal typing stops working and the HIToolbox trace returns.
N3.label: N3 failure isolated to packaged application

symptoms_visible: With the bundle identifier changed from org.alacritty to alacritty, the packaged application accepts normal typing.
With the original org.alacritty identifier, typing does not work.
Pressing ´ and § together temporarily lets me type, but input stops again after the application loses focus.
N4.label: N4 bundle-identity-specific workaround found

symptoms_visible: After reformatting the machine and performing a clean macOS installation, Alacritty accepts normal typing again.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved after clean system installation

question_patterns: Can you launch the executable with --print-events and --config-file=/dev/null and share the complete output from the start?
Does the behavior remain when you explicitly use /dev/null as the configuration file?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I ran /Applications/Alacritty.app/Contents/MacOS/alacritty --print-events --config-file=/dev/null. It loads /dev/null, but I still cannot type and the complete log starts printing HIToolbox and AppKit stack traces shortly after initialization.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Using /dev/null fixes it completely, and typing works normally with no HIToolbox trace.
The same failure occurs with /dev/null, but the window and display dimensions in the log are different.

question_patterns: Are you running any special software that interacts with macOS windowing or the Apple UI stack?
Do you use window-management or injection software in this setup?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I have been using Yabai alongside Alacritty, and it requires SIP to be partially disabled. I am not sure whether that is the kind of Apple-stack interaction you mean.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: This is a clean macOS installation with no window manager, injection software, or modified SIP settings.

edges.comment: From c4-c7 on the reporter's system: the handler requested a /dev/null event run and asked about software interacting with the Apple stack; the reporter supplied the raw log behavior and disclosed Yabai with partially disabled SIP.

solution.intent: Disable Yabai to test whether its macOS window-management integration is preventing Alacritty from receiving keyboard input.
solution.concrete_example: Stop the Yabai services, relaunch Alacritty, and check whether normal keyboard input returns.

edges.comment: From c8-c10 on the reporter's system: the reporter stopped the Yabai services through Brew, but the input failure remained. This falsifies simply stopping Yabai as the fix, though it does not establish what other system integration might remain.

question_patterns: Do older Alacritty versions accept normal typing in the same setup?
Can you try the latest stable 0.11 build and report whether input works?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The latest stable 0.11 does work and I can type in it, although on macOS I need the newer winit Option-key fixes.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Alacritty 0.11 has exactly the same input failure.

question_patterns: Can you run a winit keyboard example and report whether it emits keyboard events or the same unusual trace?
When typing in the winit example window, do you see KeyboardInput or ReceivedCharacter output?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In the affected winit example I could not see the characters I wrote, and it printed a HIToolbox/AppKit trace like Alacritty.

question_patterns: Please test the latest winit master example and paste the raw keyboard output.
Does the current winit master example print KeyboardInput and ReceivedCharacter when you type?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Latest winit master works as expected. It prints KeyboardInput entries and ReceivedCharacter lines such as 'u', 'y', and 'g' when I type.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Latest winit master also prints the HIToolbox trace and never emits ReceivedCharacter.
Latest master emits the same keyboard and character events, but I typed different letters.

edges.comment: From c11-c22 on the reporter's system: older Alacritty and multiple winit examples were tested. The answers preserve the reporter's raw observations rather than claiming that a particular winit change is the root cause.

question_patterns: Can you run the Alacritty branch with the updated winit dependency directly through cargo and report whether typing works?
Please launch the candidate branch with cargo run and test keyboard input.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Running the updated branch directly with cargo run works and I am able to type into it.

question_patterns: Does cargo run --release also accept normal typing?
Can you compare the release-mode binary launched by cargo with the packaged application?
If you package that same source as Alacritty.app and copy it to Applications, can you still type?
Is the behavior different between the directly launched binary and the generated .app bundle?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The binary launched through cargo works, but after make app and copying target/release/osx/Alacritty.app to /Applications, I cannot type. The packaged app prints the HIToolbox trace again.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both cargo run --release and the generated Alacritty.app fail in exactly the same way.
The generated app fails from another folder as well as from /Applications, while the cargo-launched binary works.

edges.comment: From c23-c29 on the reporter's system: testing the candidate dependency update exposed a packaging-dependent difference. The same code accepted input through cargo, including release mode, but not as the generated application bundle.

question_patterns: Which exact macOS version are you using?
Can you provide the full macOS version number?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I use the latest Ventura, version 13.2.1.

solution.intent: Inspect and compare the packaged application's Info.plist because the directly launched release binary works while the .app bundle does not; test whether the bundle identity is what triggers the input failure.
solution.concrete_example: Compare the generated app's Info.plist with the working form. On this machine, changing CFBundleIdentifier from org.alacritty to alacritty makes normal keyboard input work; restoring org.alacritty reproduces the problem.

edges.comment: From c30-c43 on the reporter's system: the handler pointed to the plist as the meaningful packaging difference. The reporter experimented with it and later identified the exact observable trigger: org.alacritty failed, while the renamed identifier worked. The temporary ´+§ behavior was also reported by the same user.

solution.intent: Treat the failure as machine-specific macOS state associated with the original application identity, with the exact responsible rule or software left unidentified; reset that system state and verify Alacritty input afterward.
solution.concrete_example: The org.alacritty bundle identity triggered the failure only in the existing macOS environment. Renaming the identifier was a workaround; the reporter ultimately reformatted the machine, performed a clean macOS installation, and confirmed that normal Alacritty input returned. The thread did not identify the exact stale rule or third-party component responsible.
solution.inference_hint: The evidence supports only a machine-specific macOS state tied to the org.alacritty application identity: the same release code works through cargo, changing the bundle identifier restores input, and a clean OS installation removes the failure. The thread never establishes which rule, cache, security setting, or third-party program caused that state. A later different user reported that uninstalling Fig fixed a similar symptom, but the original reporter never confirmed having Fig, so Fig must not be asserted as this reporter's root cause.

edges.comment: From c44-c47 on the reporter's system: no matching rule was located and the maintainer did not identify a precise macOS mechanism. The reporter then reformatted the machine, installed macOS cleanly, and confirmed the problem was gone. c49 is from a different affected user who mentions Fig; it is not spliced into the original reporter's causal chain.

satisfaction_conditions: Must characterize the accepted diagnosis no more specifically than the evidence permits: the failure was tied to the reporter's prior macOS environment and the org.alacritty application identity, while the exact responsible rule, cache, security state, or third-party component remained unknown.

Must ground the diagnosis in the packaging evidence: cargo-run binaries accepted input, the packaged application did not, and changing CFBundleIdentifier from org.alacritty to alacritty restored normal input.

Must not present deleting the Alacritty configuration, stopping Yabai, or merely updating winit as the confirmed fix; each was insufficient to explain or resolve the packaged-app failure in this case.
Must not claim Fig was the original reporter's root cause; Fig was mentioned only by a different user after the reporter had already resolved the issue through a clean system installation.
Must treat the reporter's clean macOS installation as the confirmed resolution and require verification that normal typing works afterward before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical macOS user who can build Rust projects, run cargo examples, inspect application bundles, edit Info.plist, and follow git testing instructions, but needs guidance with bisection and macOS internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Informal and cooperative, with short replies and pasted logs; tests suggestions quickly, reports surprising distinctions between launch methods, and asks direct follow-up questions when instructions are unclear.
